_comment: Colorado 2025-2026 Housing Tax Credit QAP, Second Amendment, CHFA. The handoff flagged Colorado for having few 'point' mentions; the scoring is in the document after all, in Section 5 Scoring Criteria, PDF pp.44-50 (printed pp.40-46; the printed page is four lower). Page numbers are PDF page indices. NO MAXIMUM IS STATED. The floors are stated: 130 points for federal 9%, 115 for federal 4% with state credit, 95 for federal 4% (p.44, and as Threshold #1 on p.20). Hand-summed before loading, the itemised maxima give 220.5. That is 92.5 for the weighted targeting formula, a ceiling computed from its stated weights; 20 for the lowest-AMI county bonus; 15 for either 5.A.1(d) or 5.B.5, which cannot combine; 40 extended use; 1 revitalization plan; 6 location; 39 project characteristics; 5 applicant; and 2 waitlist. The loader matched. Housing Need Characteristics (5.B.1) is excluded from the total because its point values live in Application exhibits C-1 and C-2, not the QAP. The computed figure is therefore a ceiling with one criterion missing, and it leans on a derived number: read it as structure, not as a stated maximum. Thresholds are in CO_thresholds.json.

track_totals.note: No maximum stated. Computed 220.5 excludes 5.B.1 Housing Need (values in Application exhibits C-1/C-2) and uses 92.5 as the targeting formula's ceiling, computed from its stated weights (84.5 without project-based assistance). Floors: 130 (9%), 115 (4% + state), 95 (4%). Because 9% projects must elect 25 years of extended use, their 40 points under 5.A.2 are effectively automatic, so the 130 floor is met largely by targeting.

groups.label: Extremely low-income targeting or homeless/special populations
groups.source_quote: Projects claiming points in this section cannot also claim points under Section 5.B.5.
groups.note: 5.A.1(d) says it cannot be combined with 5.B.5, and 5.B.5 says the same of 5.A.1(d). Both are worth 15.

criteria.heading: Low-income targeting (weighted AMI score)
criteria.quote: a weight factor of 92.5 for selecting the 40 percent
criteria.note: Share of rent-restricted units at each AMI level times a weight: 50 at 60% AMI, 72.5 at 50%, 92.5 at 40%, summed, under whichever minimum set-aside (20/50, 40/60 or Average Income) the project elects. No maximum is stated. The 92.5 recorded here is the formula's ceiling, all rent-restricted units at the 40% weight, which the plan permits only with project-based rental assistance or operating subsidies; otherwise no more than 60% of low-income units may count at 40%, which caps the score at 84.5 (0.6 x 92.5 + 0.4 x 72.5). Both ceilings are computed from the stated weights, not stated by CHFA. A primary criterion: a project must earn points here and in 5.A.2 to be eligible at all.

criteria.heading: Additional points for counties with lowest AMI
criteria.quote: 20 additional points for counties with lowest AMI
criteria.note: Printed on each of the three set-aside worksheets. Which counties count as 'lowest AMI' is not defined in the QAP beyond using the current county median income at application.

criteria.heading: Extremely low-income targeting (30% AMI)
criteria.quote: Additional points will be awarded for projects that target extremely low-income residents.

tiers.tier_label: 10% of units at or below 30% AMI

criteria.note: Bonus points on top of the chosen set-aside table. Cannot be combined with 5.B.5; see the group. Homeless and special population projects need five years' development experience and supportive services from a provider with three years' experience.

criteria.heading: Extended low-income use
criteria.quote: 15 Years of Compliance + 25 Years of Extended Use – 40 points
criteria.note: Federal 9% and competitive state credit projects are already required to elect 25 years of extended use, so for them the 40 points are effectively automatic; only 4% projects choose between 25 and 40. A primary criterion.

criteria.heading: Community revitalization plan
criteria.quote: CHFA will award one point for projects located in a qualified census tract that contribute to a Community
criteria.note: Requires measurable community impact and significant local government funding or major investment beyond tax credit housing.

criteria.detail_external: Preliminary Application exhibits C-1 and C-2
